transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-08-15
Start time: 16:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Avery Chen, Marcus Patel, Lina Torres (Redwood) — Diana Morales, Ethan Cho, Priya Raman, Samir Gupta (Northbridge)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Quick review of Northbridge vendor questionnaire. Focus on evidence and next steps. Some clarifications on private deployment and KMS/HSM.

[00:00] Avery Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time. Um, we've got — Marcus and I will walk through the vendor form you sent and map it back to our SIG/CAIQ export. Diana, do you want to quickly confirm scope?
[00:12] Diana Morales: Yeah thanks Avery. Hi all. The main ask is that we map the vendor form fields to Redwood's controls and provide evidence for SOC 2, ISO questions. We also have a handful of questions about SSO, RBAC scoping, and how audit logs are retained, retention periods and exportability.
[00:27] Marcus Patel: Great — totally. Quick note, I'll refer to our CAIQ export as the canonical mapping; we also have a custom evidence pack for SOC 2 that matches the control IDs. Uh, one thing I want to confirm up front: are you planning to put any production data in a Redwood Private (VPC) deployment or use hosted?
[00:42] Ethan Cho: At this stage, we want to evaluate private deployment for prod because of residency requirements — some datasets need to stay in the EU region. For POC we can use hosted.
[00:50] Avery Chen: Makes sense. We'll flag the differences — hosted vs private have different evidence for network controls, egress controls, and customer-managed KMS.
[01:05] Priya Raman: Also procurement is interested in timelines — when can we expect the evidence to be delivered?
[01:10] Avery Chen: We'll put expected dates in the action items. Marcus, want to pull up the CAIQ mapping?
[01:16] Marcus Patel: Yep. So starting with the questionnaire, question 2.1 asks about encryption at rest, key management. Short answer: we support envelope encryption with customer-managed keys in private deployments and KMS integrations for hosted. Our hosted KMS uses cloud KMS providers; for Private we can integrate with your KMS/H-S-M via customer-provisioned keys.
[01:36] Samir Gupta: When you say HSM, do you mean you support BYO-HSM or you use a managed HSM? We need details for FIPS-140 compliance.
[01:44] Marcus Patel: Right. For hosted we use cloud KMS which is backed by provider HSMs; for Private there's an option to connect to your HSM via standard KMIP or to use customer-managed key material in the config. I'll include the exact details in the evidence pack — and point to our FIPS note.
[01:59] Diana Morales: Do you have SOC 2 Type II? And is ISO 27001 certificate available? The form requests dates and the auditor firm.
[02:07] Lina Torres: Yes — we are SOC 2 Type II for the inference runtime and control plane; certificate and the audit firm info we will share. ISO 27001 is in progress for the platform team — we can provide the scope document.
[02:18] Diana Morales: Okay, please include scope boundaries.
[02:22] Marcus Patel: Noted. Next section is identity and access. Your form asks about SSO providers and SAML/SCIM support. We support SAML 2.0 for SSO, SCIM for user provisioning, and RBAC with granular roles. For Dedicated/Open Private customers you can plug in an IdP via SAML OIDC as well.
[02:44] Ethan Cho: Does role separation extend to model-level permissions? We need to ensure developers can't exfiltrate customer data via prompts.
[02:52] Marcus Patel: Good question. Our RBAC model supports resource-scoped roles: you can restrict model invocation at project or team level, and limit access to logs and audit exports. There's also masking for prompt logs; however prompts used in hosted inference may be logged to help services — we can configure redaction or bypass logging in Private setups.
[03:16] Diana Morales: On logging, what's the retention and can we pull raw logs for our SIEM?
[03:21] Marcus Patel: By default hosted retention is 90 days for detailed logs and 365 days for high-level audit trail; we can extend retention via add-on. We provide log export endpoints and S3 sinks for audit logs which you can ingest into Splunk or your SIEM. For Private, logs remain within your VPC and you control retention and forwarding.
[03:42] Priya Raman: You mentioned redaction. The questionnaire has a question about whether user-provided PII is ever stored unencrypted. Can you explicitly say where prompt text is stored and for how long?
[03:52] Avery Chen: Prompt text for hosted inference is stored transiently for a short period for debugging and safety purposes; we've got a default of 7 days for full transcripts and 90 days aggregated metrics — we'll provide the exact policy doc. For Private, you can opt out of retention entirely. We'll include a statement for the questionnaire.
[04:13] Samir Gupta: Are keys physically controlled by Redwood for hosted? We need to know key custody.
[04:18] Marcus Patel: For hosted keys are managed by the cloud provider's KMS; Redwood does not have access to the plaintext keys. For private deployments you can bring your own KMS/HSM so you maintain custody. We'll add language clarifying zero-access key policies.
[04:36] Diana Morales: The form includes a section on network segmentation and egress controls — can you provide firewall rules and port lists?
[04:43] Marcus Patel: Yes, for private we will produce a network diagram and egress port list. For hosted we can provide a published IP range and an explanation of outbound connection policies. I'll write that up and attach to the evidence pack.
[05:00] Avery Chen: One quick note — we've had a couple of customers misread our KV cache reference as some sort of external K-V cash store, so in the mapping we'll clarify KV cache is ephemeral inference state kept in memory/GPU and not persisted by default.
[05:14] Diana Morales: (laughs) good to know.
[05:17] [00:05:20] Priya Raman: There's a procurement item about indemnity/contractual language tied to data residency — if we choose hosted with EU region, is there a guarantee that data won't be replicated outside EU?
[05:30] Avery Chen: We can contractually commit to region residency for customer content in hosted by using region pinning with contractual addendum. For Private deployments it's under your control. We'll loop in legal on exact wording.
[05:41] [00:06:15] Ethan Cho: On the SIG/CAIQ mapping — if you map an item to 'N/A' what's the recommended evidence to close that gap?
[05:49] Marcus Patel: We'll provide compensating controls where applicable — e.g., if a vendor form asks about physical access to co-lo racks for hosted, we'll map to provider controls and our vendor due-diligence. But we'll annotate each mapping with either 'evidence attached', 'control description', or 'compensating control'.
[06:05] Diana Morales: Do you have pen test reports and vuln scan cadence? They ask for last penetration test date and remediation cycle.
[06:12] Lina Torres: Yes — annual penetration tests, last one was 2026-06-10, and our remediation SLA is tracked with triage and fix windows; we'll include the executive summary and remediation attestations.
[06:25] Samir Gupta: For integration/API keys — is there support for rotating keys and restricting scopes?
[06:30] Marcus Patel: API keys can be scoped to specific routes/models and rotated via the console or API. We'll show the rotation APIs and the audit trail entries for key use.
[06:45] [00:07:05] Priya Raman: On the privacy questions — does Redwood perform any model training on customer prompts or usage data?
[06:51] Avery Chen: No. We do not use customer-provided prompts to train public models. We have an explicit policy and can provide signed attestation. For some service analytics we may use anonymized, aggregated metrics unless you opt out.
[07:06] Diana Morales: Audit logging — can you export immutable logs? The customer form asks about WORM buckets or tamper-evident storage.
[07:14] Marcus Patel: For hosted we can export to customer-controlled S3 with object lock enabled to achieve WORM-like behavior. For Private, obviously, you can configure the storage solution to meet WORM requirements. We'll document the S3 export mechanism and suggest configuration patterns.
[07:33] [00:08:10] Ethan Cho: There's a question about change control and vulnerability disclosure — do you have a published process and PGP key for security reports?
[07:40] Lina Torres: Yes, we have a published security disclosure process and a PGP key. We'll provide the link and the contact.
[07:48] Priya Raman: Something specific on the questionnaire: they want a list of sub-processors or third parties with access to customer data. Can you list cloud provider, monitoring, and any data processors?
[07:58] Marcus Patel: We'll provide a sub-processor list and a data flow diagram. For hosted the main processor is the cloud provider for infra, plus our monitoring vendor; we also use a customer analytics vendor for aggregated metrics — we'll list versions and access scopes.
[08:14] Diana Morales: Question about SLA and incident notification timing. The form expects RTO/RPO and P1/P2 notification windows.
[08:20] Avery Chen: Our SLA for Dedicated has 99.9% uptime with specified latency targets; incident notifications for Sev1 are within 15 minutes via pager and follow-up reports within 24 hours. We'll attach the SLA doc.
[08:34] [00:09:10] Samir Gupta: For the cryptography section — can you confirm algorithms and key lengths used for at-rest and in-transit encryption? We need cipher suites and TLS versions.
[08:43] Marcus Patel: Sure — TLS 1.2+ and recommended TLS 1.3, AES-256 for at-rest, RSA/ECDSA for cert signing depending on provider. We'll include a crypto spec in the evidence pack.
[08:56] Diana Morales: The vendor questionnaire has a checkbox for 'data residency guarantee via contract' — can you confirm if Redwood will accept a contractual clause to keep customer content in EU only?
[09:05] Avery Chen: We can accept region residency clauses for hosted with region pinning and contractual addendum. We'll route legal to discuss precise wording.
[09:12] [00:10:00] Priya Raman: A few of the customer's security folks also asked about background checks for personnel with access to production; do you do SOC or background screening?
[09:20] Lina Torres: Yes, we perform background checks for employees with privileged access and maintain HR attestations; we'll provide a summary and role lists for the SOC auditors.
[09:31] Marcus Patel: Jumping to the question about encryption key audit — we also surface key usage logs to customers for private KMS integrations and for hosted we provide key usage metadata via the cloud provider's audit logs.
[09:48] [00:10:55] Ethan Cho: If we choose a private deployment, how are upgrades handled? We need maintenance windows, rollback procedures, and assurance that model weights are not transmitted externally.
[10:02] Marcus Patel: For private deployments upgrades are planned with you; we provide upgrade bundles and a canary rollout model. Model weights for private deployments are pre-provisioned to the cluster — we can do air-gapped transfers if required and document the checksum/manifesting process. For hosted model distribution we use signed artifacts and verify signatures on the runtime.
[10:22] Diana Morales: Good. On the evidence itself — the questionnaire expects specific file types and paths; can you provide a zipped package and also a spreadsheet mapping questions to evidence files?
[10:31] Avery Chen: Yes — we'll produce a SIG/CAIQ export CSV and a mapping spreadsheet with links to evidence PDFs. That will go into the shared drive.
[10:39] [00:11:30] Priya Raman: Are there any 'red flags' we should be aware of that could slow procurement? For example, do you historically have customers who required additional on-site audits?
[10:48] Lina Torres: Occasionally customers request on-site audits for Dedicated/private but it's rare. The typical blockers are specific contractual language on data residency or additional indemnity clauses — those can slow legal. We'll try to pre-empt by sharing standard contract language.
[11:03] Samir Gupta: For the logging question again — can you show a sample audit log entry schema? That helps our SIEM mapping.
[11:10] Marcus Patel: We'll attach a sample JSON entry and an example Splunk ingest mapping.
[11:16] [00:12:00] Diana Morales: Do you have any certifications for cloud provider supply chain, or do you do vendor risk checks on your dependencies? The questionnaire asks about vendor risk management.
[11:24] Avery Chen: We conduct vendor due diligence and have a vendor risk program; we also rely on provider attestations and will include a summary of that program.
[11:33] [00:12:35] Ethan Cho: For throughput and latency SLOs — procurement asked if any changes to service could impact latency without notice? We need assurances about breaking changes and customer notification policy.
[11:43] Marcus Patel: Breaking changes are handled with deprecation notices and a minimum notice period for API changes; we'll include the deprecation policy and the console's change log. For performance-impacting changes we coordinate with customers on Dedicated and provide change windows.
[11:58] [00:13:20] Priya Raman: The questionnaire's legal section asks for a data processing addendum (DPA) — can you provide the standard DPA and confirm subprocessor list?
[12:08] Lina Torres: We'll attach the DPA and the subprocessor addendum.
[12:14] [00:13:50] Diana Morales: Ok, let's capture concrete next steps so procurement and security have clarity.
[12:20] Avery Chen: Sure. Action items: we'll produce a SIG export + mapping spreadsheet and evidence pack by Wednesday (2026-08-18). Marcus will prepare the network/VPC diagram and crypto spec by 2026-08-25. We'll share SOC 2 certificate and penetration test executive summary immediately after the call.
[12:36] Priya Raman: That timeline should work. We'll review and come back with any follow-up questions and prioritize the procurement checklist.
[12:44] [00:14:30] Samir Gupta: One last tech nit: how do you handle model snapshots and access control for model artifacts? Does Redwood permit restricting who can pull model artifacts?
[12:54] Marcus Patel: Yes, model artifacts can be scoped by team and repository permissions; for private we can limit distribution to a signed manifest and CNC — we'll include the model artifact access policy doc.
[13:07] Diana Morales: Great. Thanks everyone.
[13:10] Avery Chen: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the pack and schedule the technical deep dive.
[13:15] [End of recording — approximate 48 minutes]

- Legal to be looped for DPA and residency clause language.
